# util-memory - context for bug hunters

Scope: `jix/src/util/aligned_vec/{mod.rs,raw.rs}`, `jix/src/util/{arrayvec.rs,buf_pool.rs,bitmap.rs,cpu_cache.rs,hint.rs}`,
`jix/src/util/mod.rs:1-821`. Paths below are relative to `jix/src/` unless they start with `jix/` or `jix-py/`.

Facts that change how to read this code:
- Release builds have overflow checks OFF (no `[profile.release]` override in `jix/Cargo.toml`): unchecked `*`/`+`
  wrap silently in shipped wheels; only debug/test builds panic.
- CI tests only on ubuntu x86_64 (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml:18`) and never runs Miri (the `cfg(miri)` stubs in
  codec/cpu_cache are unused by CI). x86 (32-bit) and armv7 wheels are built (`.github/workflows/release.yaml:88-180`) but never tested.

## Purpose
Low-level pieces every storage/op path stands on: an aligned growable byte vector (`AlignedBytes`, a fork of the
aligned-vec crate) and its raw allocation (`RawAlignedBytes`); a fixed-capacity stack vector `ArrayVec` (backs
`DimArray<T> = ArrayVec<T, 8>` at dimension.rs:516, the dtype inner shape, filter lists); the per-`ReadContext`
scratch allocator `BufferPool`/`PoolBuf`; a u8 per-dim flag set `DimBitmap`; cache-size detection and
`CACHE_LINE_SIZE`; branch hints; and util/mod.rs helpers (stride/span arithmetic, slice reinterpretation,
`AlternatingBuffers` for codec filter ping-pong, the read-tile heuristic `scale_read_shape`, the `noalias` pointer
wrappers used by every hot inner loop, raw POD I/O).

## Contracts

### RawAlignedBytes (util/aligned_vec/raw.rs)
- Invariant: `capacity > 0` means `ptr` came from `alloc`/`realloc` with `Layout(capacity, align)`; `capacity == 0`
  means `ptr` is the provenance-less dangling address `align` (raw.rs:45) and Drop does nothing (raw.rs:20).
  Fields are `pub` (raw.rs:7-9) and the type is re-exported `pub(crate)` (util/mod.rs:2); only aligned_vec and
  buf_pool.rs use it, through methods.
- `new_unchecked`, `with_capacity_unchecked[_zeroed]` (raw.rs:44,53,70): documented precondition `align` is a
  power of two (so >= 1). Caller-established; `is_valid_alloc` only debug_asserts it (raw.rs:246) and computes
  `align - 1`. Size > `isize::MAX - (align-1)` panics via `capacity_overflow` (raw.rs:32,194); null alloc gives
  `handle_alloc_error`.
- `grow_amortized` / `grow_exact` (raw.rs:84,118): pub unsafe, undocumented. Need `len <= capacity`,
  `additional > 0` (debug_assert only), and for grow_exact `len + additional > capacity` (else realloc shrinks).
  Established by `AlignedBytes::reserve`, `reserve_exact`, `push` (aligned_vec/mod.rs:193-211, 260-263).
  The capacity==0 path ignores `len` (fine only because len <= capacity == 0).
- `shrink_to(len)` (raw.rs:144): needs `0 < len < capacity`; only `len < capacity` is debug_asserted.
- Send + Sync (raw.rs:13,15): "unique owner of a plain byte allocation, like Box<[u8]>".

### AlignedBytes (util/aligned_vec/mod.rs)
- Provides `as_slice/as_mut_slice` over `[0, len)` (mod.rs:237-256), base aligned to `alignment()`;
  `new_padded`/`with_capacity_padded` raise alignment to `CACHE_LINE_SIZE` (mod.rs:109-136).
- Relies on a non-zero power-of-two align. `RuntimeAlign::new` (mod.rs:27-36) panics on non-powers of two but
  ACCEPTS 0; the doc at mod.rs:46-48 ("0 uses the minimum alignment") is stale aligned-vec text.
- `set_len` (mod.rs:374): pub unsafe, undocumented. Real contract: `new_len <= capacity` and every byte of
  `[0,new_len)` written before it is read. Production callers set the length over UNINITIALIZED memory and pass
  `as_mut_slice()` to a writer: codec/mod.rs:159-171 (filter scratch), array.rs:1368-1369, 1404-1405, 1432-1435.
- Used outside tests: `new_exact`, `new_padded`, `with_capacity_exact`, `from_slice`, `clone`, `clear`,
  `reserve`, `set_len`, `as_*slice`, slice `fill`. `shrink_to*`, `append`, `resize`, `from_iter`,
  `into_raw_parts/from_raw_parts` are dead outside tests (`#![allow(unused)]`, mod.rs:1). All live callers pass an
  `Alignment`-derived value (dtype.rs:65-95 guarantees 1..=32768 power of two) or `max(_, CACHE_LINE_SIZE)`.

### BufferPool / PoolBuf (util/buf_pool.rs)
- `get(size, alignment)` (buf_pool.rs:40): capacity `>= size`, base aligned to `max(alignment, CACHE_LINE_SIZE)`;
  bytes are UNINITIALIZED (fresh `alloc`, not zeroed) or STALE from a previous user (doc buf_pool.rs:34-39).
- `PoolBuf::as_slice/as_mut_slice` (buf_pool.rs:107-119) span the WHOLE capacity, possibly > `size` (behavior
  introduced by commit 763a701; before it the slice was exactly `size`). Callers must slice to `size` where length
  matters (doc buf_pool.rs:97-100). Callers: codec/mod.rs:276-279, codec/filter/bit_shuffle.rs:121-122,160-161,
  ops/reduction.rs:502-504, storage/compact.rs:397-398 (all slice to size); storage/elementwise_pipeline.rs:516
  (Staging: whole slice used as an nd_copy dst with explicit n); elementwise_pipeline.rs:878 and
  storage/buf.rs:311-316 wrap it in `StridedBuf::from_pool`, whose `data()/data_mut()` return the full capacity
  minus offset (storage/buf.rs:170,180).
- Distinct live PoolBufs never overlap (a buffer is either in a free list or owned by one PoolBuf). Callers rely
  on this for their noalias claims (e.g. Staging vs output buffer).
- `BufferPool` is `!Sync` (UnsafeCell) and `Send` (ReadContext asserted Send, codec/mod.rs:459-462). `PoolBuf<'a>`
  holds `&'a BufferPool`: neither Send nor Sync, cannot outlive the pool.
- Reentrancy: the `&mut Vec` built from the UnsafeCell (buf_pool.rs:42,55,72) lives only across one pop/push/insert;
  nothing in between can re-enter the pool (alloc failure aborts). The `*mut Vec` that `get_pool` returns into
  `align_other` is invalidated by the next `align_other.insert` (buf_pool.rs:87); it is used immediately.
- `size` arithmetic is the caller's: e.g. `product * itemsize` at storage/buf.rs:311-314 and
  elementwise_pipeline.rs:875-878, `chunk_len_max * itemsize` at :516. A wrapped product yields a too-small buffer
  while the strides still describe the full shape.

### ArrayVec / DimArray (util/arrayvec.rs)
- CAP <= 255 (`len: u8`); `new()` asserts at runtime (arrayvec.rs:30-35). Instances: CAP 8 (DimArray), 4 (DtypeShape,
  dtype.rs:130; filters, codec/mod.rs:48), 2 (storage/info.rs:71-74).
- `len()` feeds `assert_unchecked(len <= CAP)` (arrayvec.rs:57): any stored len > CAP is UB, not a panic.
  `set_len` (pub unsafe, :183) only debug_asserts and truncates `as u8`; `push_unchecked` (pub unsafe, :95) requires
  not-full (assert_unchecked). No caller outside the file uses either. `push` (:87), `insert` (:143-150),
  `extend`/`FromIterator` (:412-414), `insert_first_const` (:171) assert. `dim_arr` asserts `ndim <= NDIM_MAX`
  (dimension.rs:526); `try_dim_arr` panics via collect (dimension.rs:544).
- `extend_from_slice` (pub(super), :431) debug_asserts fit and silently TRUNCATES in release; its callers
  (from_slice :47, clone_from :572, IntoIter::clone :334) pre-check.
- `[0,len)` initialized; `truncate` lowers len before dropping the tail; `IntoIter` Drop zeroes len first (:313-325).
  No pop/remove/drain: other mutation goes through `DerefMut` slices.

### DimBitmap (util/bitmap.rs)
- Invariant `len <= 8` and bits at positions >= len are zero (derived PartialEq/Hash at bitmap.rs:12 depend on it).
  Every constructor/mutator asserts (bitmap.rs:33,51,58,78,91); `len()` uses `assert_unchecked` (:44).

### cpu_cache / hint
- `cache_sizes()` (cpu_cache.rs:57) guarantees `l1_data <= l2 <= l3` (:77-78) but NOT non-zero: Linux `"0K"`
  parses to 0 (parse_size :144-154); macOS rejects 0 (:225). Consumers: storage/params.rs:328 (`block_size =
  l1_data`, then `/ itemsize`), :379-381.
- `CACHE_LINE_SIZE` (:326) is a per-arch constant: 128 x86_64/aarch64, 64 x86, 32 armv7.
- `likely/unlikely` (hint.rs) are identity functions.

### util/mod.rs helpers
- `strided_span_bytes` (mod.rs:109): bytes from base to the end of the furthest element: sum `stride*(len-1)` +
  itemsize; 0 if any dim is 0; itemsize for 0-d. Unchecked arithmetic; `zip` ignores extra entries if lengths differ.
  Sizes slices for `StridedBuf::from_raw_parts[_mut]` (storage/buf.rs:70,90) and `PtrMutNoalias::new`
  (elementwise_pipeline.rs:280-283, 413-416): an underestimate is an out-of-provenance access.
- `default_strides*` (mod.rs:121-149, 177-186): C-order byte strides, unchecked multiply. `default_strides`
  converts through `Idx::from_u64`, a truncating `as` cast (mod.rs:86-88): u64 shapes to usize on 32-bit.
- `strides_for_layout_order` (mod.rs:159): REQUIRES `layout_order` to be a permutation of `0..ndim` (only the
  length is debug_asserted, :165). Only then do the strides fit in `product(shape)*itemsize` bytes - exactly what
  materialize_out_buf allocates (storage/buf.rs:311-316). Nobody validates the permutation
  (ArraySpecDynamic::new, storage/params.rs:753-771); producers: storage/plain.rs:180, ops/shape_ops/{stack,
  remove_dim,reshape,insert_dim}.rs, ops/reduction.rs:179.
- `cast_slice/cast_slice_mut<T,U>` (mod.rs:193-213): checks U-alignment, `size_of::<U>() > 0`, byte multiple.
  Caller must ensure the bytes are initialized and valid as U (and, for `_mut`, writes keep T valid). Undocumented.
- `AlternatingBuffers` (mod.rs:291-403): `edit()` returns `(src, dst)` with dst a WHOLE scratch buffer. Init state:
  first dst is tmp_buf1; `new(main, secondary)`: first dst is `secondary`. `data()/into_data()` return the whole
  last-written buffer (no written length); callers make every buffer exactly the payload length
  (codec/mod.rs:159-171, 276-279).
- `scale_read_shape` (mod.rs:468, doc :443-467): every dim in `scale_order` ends in `[1, max(max_shape[d],1)]`
  or is snapped to `max(array_shape[d],1)`; unlisted dims untouched. Panics if `scale_order` yields > 8 items
  (collect at :483) or an index >= ndim. Callers: storage/params.rs:740, array.rs:1330.
- `SendSyncPtr<T>` (mod.rs:529-542): unconditional Send+Sync for any T; `new` is unsafe with no stated contract.
  Callers: storage/plain.rs:187 (kept alive by `allocation: A`), archive/block.rs:498 (into an `Arc<Mmap>`,
  dereferenced by `MmapData::as_ref`, storage/block.rs:445).
- `assert_unchecked_eq!` (mod.rs:544-549): release UB if false. Uses: ops/op2.rs:181, ops/into_type.rs:88,103,
  storage/block.rs:216.
- `value_as_bytes<T>` (mod.rs:553): T must have no padding (callers: padding-free repr(C) Header/Section,
  archive/common.rs:46, archive/block.rs:168,251). `value_from_io<T>` (mod.rs:571): T valid for every bit
  pattern; reads into an uninitialized buffer through an arbitrary `impl Read`.
- `calc_block_end(begin,end,b)` (mod.rs:609): exclusive end block; `begin/b` for empty ranges; div-by-zero if b==0.
- `PtrNoalias::new(ptr, span)` / `PtrMutNoalias::new` (mod.rs:674,722): slice::from_raw_parts(_mut) contract:
  non-null, valid for `span` bytes, and for all of `'a` nothing writes the range (PtrNoalias) / nothing else
  accesses it (PtrMutNoalias). `as_ptr/as_mut_ptr` carry provenance ONLY over the wrapped span: a kernel touching
  bytes past `span` is UB even inside the same allocation. `from_slice` makes the same claim from a borrow.
  `bytes_offset(off)` needs `off <= span` (get_unchecked; caught only by debug ub_checks).
- `read_maybe_aligned::<true>` / `write_maybe_aligned::<true>` (mod.rs:762-793) need alignment. `REQUIRE_ALIGNED`
  (mod.rs:641) is false on x86/x86_64/aarch64 and TRUE elsewhere, incl. shipped armv7: there every
  `::<REQUIRE_ALIGNED>` access must be aligned, so caller checks are load-bearing (ops/where_op.rs:192-197,
  ops/reduction.rs:699; elementwise_pipeline.rs:610-612 and :839-841 are debug_assert only).

## Unsafe inventory
- raw.rs:13,15 Send/Sync impls - sound if fields are never shared-mutated (no interior mutability). Local.
- raw.rs:22-27 Drop dealloc with `from_size_align_unchecked(capacity, align)` - assumes alloc layout == current
  fields. Relies on every mutator (grow/shrink) updating both; pub fields make this non-local.
- raw.rs:45 `null.wrapping_add(align)` + `NonNull::new_unchecked` - needs align != 0. NOT established
  (RuntimeAlign::new admits 0); holds today only because every caller passes >= 1.
- raw.rs:58,76,198,212 alloc paths - size > 0 (checked by the capacity==0 branch), align power of two (caller).
- raw.rs:105-115, 131-141, 232-234 realloc paths - old layout matches, new size > 0 and valid (is_valid_alloc).
- raw.rs:152-158 shrink realloc - new size `len` may be 0; result not null-checked. NOT established.
- aligned_vec/mod.rs:97-102,118-126 safe ctors wrap the unsafe raw ctors - unsound for align 0 (see above).
- aligned_vec/mod.rs:243,255 slices over `[0,len)` - assumes init; relies on set_len callers (non-local).
- aligned_vec/mod.rs:266-270,336,353,362,383,411-425,436 raw writes - capacity ensured by a preceding reserve /
  with_capacity in the same function. Local.
- buf_pool.rs:42,55,72 `&mut *UnsafeCell` - exclusivity from !Sync + no reentrancy. Local but subtle.
- buf_pool.rs:45 alloc - align is an `Alignment` >= CACHE_LINE_SIZE. Local.
- buf_pool.rs:111,118 slices over full capacity - bytes may be uninit; soundness depends on every consumer
  writing before reading (non-local, see callers above).
- buf_pool.rs:124 `ManuallyDrop::take` in Drop - local, sound.
- arrayvec.rs:37,172 uninit `[MaybeUninit<T>; CAP]` - sound.
- arrayvec.rs:57 and bitmap.rs:44 `assert_unchecked(len <= CAP/8)` - relies on all writers of len (non-local for
  ArrayVec because `set_len` is crate-visible).
- arrayvec.rs:95-101 push_unchecked, :112-116 truncate, :152-163 insert (ptr::copy shift), :281-323 IntoIter
  reads/drop, :388-426 extend_from_iter (raw writes + ScopeExitGuard), :516-547 Clone (copies uninit tail for
  small trivially-droppable T) - all local index arithmetic.
- cpu_cache.rs:215-223 macOS `sysctlbyname` FFI - local.
- util/mod.rs:198-201,209-212 cast_slice(_mut) - bit validity / padding NOT checked; caller's.
- util/mod.rs:379-385 AlternatingBuffers::edit launders `&mut` through raw pointers to move the `'a` borrows out
  of `&mut self` (equivalent to `mem::take`; old refs are overwritten and never used). Not Miri-tested in CI.
- util/mod.rs:530-531 SendSyncPtr Send/Sync - caller's (`new` unsafe, undocumented).
- util/mod.rs:558 value_as_bytes, :577-582 value_from_io - padding / bit validity / uninit buffer to Read: caller's.
- util/mod.rs:676,699,724,753 PtrNoalias/PtrMutNoalias - span and aliasing claims are entirely the caller's;
  the most non-local justification in the subsystem (see Hot spots).
- util/mod.rs:769-791 aligned vs unaligned read/write - alignment is the caller's when ALIGNED.

## Edge-case surface
- Zero sizes: `PoolBuf` of size 0 pops ANY buffer (cap >= 0) or makes a dangling cap-0 one that is then pooled;
  `AlignedBytes` cap 0 uses the dangling `align` address; `strided_span_bytes` = 0 for an empty dim but =
  itemsize for 0-d; Staging spans use `n.saturating_sub(1)*stride + itemsize` (elementwise_pipeline.rs:548,574)
  which claims itemsize valid bytes even when n == 0; `cast_slice` asserts U-alignment even for an empty slice
  (dangling `1` from `Vec<u8>::new()` would panic for U with align > 1).
- 32-bit (x86, armv7): `isize::MAX` = 2 GiB caps allocations (panic, not UB); u64 shapes go to usize via `as`
  (mod.rs:86-88, array.rs:1367); span/stride/product arithmetic wraps in release; `align_of::<u64>()` is 4 on
  i686 Linux; CACHE_LINE_SIZE is 64 (x86) / 32 (armv7) so dtype alignments 64..32768 go to `align_other` lists.
- Alignment > cache line: `Alignment` allows up to 32768; buf_pool keeps one sorted free list per such alignment.
- Uninitialized memory: PoolBuf contents, `AlignedBytes::set_len` regions, `value_from_io`, padding of struct
  dtypes (dtype.rs:180-190 allows padded repr(C) structs).
- NDIM_MAX = 8: DimArray, DimBitmap, `scale_read_shape`'s `order`. ndim > 8 panics in dim_arr/collect/push.
- Cache detection: missing sysfs (containers, non-Linux/macOS, Miri) gives defaults; "0K" gives 0; duplicate
  `indexN` entries for one level: last read_dir entry wins; cpu0 may be a little core.

## Intentional behaviors
- PoolBuf slices exceed the requested size and contents are uninit/stale (buf_pool.rs:34-39, 97-100; test
  buf_pool.rs:155-157 asserts a 100-byte request gets the 256-byte buffer).
- Alignments <= CACHE_LINE_SIZE share one list allocated at CACHE_LINE_SIZE (buf_pool.rs:21,62-70; test :134-144);
  a too-small popped buffer is freed, not grown (buf_pool.rs:36-39; test :160-167); free lists for larger
  alignments are kept sorted (test :171-186). The pool is single-threaded by design (:19).
- `calc_block_end` returns `begin/block` for empty ranges (regression test util/mod.rs:846-859).
- `strided_span_bytes` sums per-dim spans; 0 for empty dims (tests util/mod.rs:1077-1123).
- `prev_power_of_two(0) == 1` (test util/mod.rs:1128).
- `scale_read_shape`: weighted dims may grow to 2x the max budget, unweighted ones stop at min, unlisted dims are
  untouched, full-coverage dims snap to `array_shape` (doc util/mod.rs:443-467; tests :963-1073).
- `ScaleWeight::new` maps any fraction in (0,1) to at least 1 (util/mod.rs:431).
- REQUIRE_ALIGNED is false where unaligned access is free (util/mod.rs:636-645).
- ArrayVec Clone copies the uninit tail for small trivially-droppable T (arrayvec.rs:527-548).
- Cache sizes: defaults 32K/256K/1M, monotonic fix-up, cpu0-only and undivided L3 (cpu_cache.rs:1-35,73-78).
- Python `numpy(out=x)` where the lazy chain reads `x` via `jix.asarray(x)` is documented UB, not checked
  (jix-py/src/array.rs:467-485) - do not report it as a new finding.

### Changed in c009869 (#87) - supersedes conflicting statements above (line numbers above refer to bb1ee2c)
- `IterExt::try_shape_product` (zero dims cannot hide an overflow) and `check_region_size`
  (32-bit) are new. `value_from_io` and the archive readers zero-fill before calling `Read` (K4).

## Hot spots
- PoolBuf full-capacity slices: does any consumer of `PoolBuf::as_*slice` or `StridedBuf::data()/data_mut()` on a
  pool-backed buffer use `.len()` as the logical size (copy_from_slice, compress, fill, length asserts)?
- Uninit reads: is every byte of a PoolBuf / `set_len` region written before read? Candidates: decode with a short
  frame, filters' tail handling, zero-padding only for partial blocks (array.rs:1406-1408), reductions that
  reuse the out buffer as state (ops/reduction.rs:495-498, 595, 1153, 1241), `cast_slice_mut::<MaybeUninit<_>,u8>` out
  buffers (array.rs:791-797).
- noalias claims: any call site where a `PtrMutNoalias` range overlaps memory read through another pointer during
  its lifetime? Look at ops/reduction.rs:495-498 ("CAREFUL: state_buf and out_ptr may alias", also :595, :1153,
  :1241) with :582 and :732-733, ops/where_op.rs:166-240 (x read into `out`, then out/y/cond wrapped), elementwise_pipeline.rs:278-285
  and 411-418 (dst vs operand cursors), nd_copy callers passing slices of one buffer as src and dst.
- Spans: are the spans passed to `PtrNoalias::new`/`PtrMutNoalias::new` always >= what the kernel touches (vector
  tails, LANES-wide reads/writes, n == 0)? `from_slice(buf.get_unchecked(off..))` patterns (array.rs:1420,
  storage/compact.rs:411,477, ops/shape_ops/flip.rs:144) need `off <= len`.
- `strides_for_layout_order`: can any producer of `read_layout_order` emit a non-permutation (duplicates, missing
  dims, wrong length after insert/remove dim)? That would turn materialize_out_buf into OOB writes.
- 32-bit: products of u64 dims cast to usize, `* itemsize` overflow, `Idx::from_u64` truncation.
- armv7 (`REQUIRE_ALIGNED`): is every aligned `read_maybe_aligned::<REQUIRE_ALIGNED>` guarded by a real (not
  debug) alignment check, including strides, not just base pointers?
- Recent churn (git log -- jix/src/util/): 763a701 rewrote PoolBuf to RawAlignedBytes with full-capacity slices
  and moved Send/Sync from AlignedBytes to RawAlignedBytes; 696eb27 rewrote scale_read_shape; 217ced2 added
  strides_for_layout_order / read_layout_order; 54878d0/01019e9 added REQUIRE_ALIGNED-based SIMD paths.

### Suspicions (unverified)
- util/aligned_vec/mod.rs:28 - `RuntimeAlign::new` admits 0, so safe `AlignedBytes::new_exact(0)` reaches
  `NonNull::new_unchecked(null)` (raw.rs:45) and `with_capacity_exact(0,n)` builds a Layout with align 0; no
  current caller passes 0.
- util/aligned_vec/raw.rs:155 - `shrink_to` reallocs to size `len`, which is 0 for shrink_to_fit/shrink_to(0) on
  an empty allocated vec (GlobalAlloc::realloc needs new_size > 0); null result unchecked (:158) and a 0-cap result
  is then leaked by Drop. Only test-reachable today.
- util/arrayvec.rs:416 - for ZST T, `extend_from_iter` skips the write but drops `elt` while counting it in len:
  double drop for a ZST with Drop (Clone forgets for this reason, :517-524). No such ArrayVec in the crate.
- util/mod.rs:578 - `value_from_io` passes an uninitialized `&mut [u8]` to an arbitrary `impl Read`
  (public `Array::read_from_reader`, archive/array.rs:145); std documents this as potential UB. Same pattern at
  archive/block.rs:452-457 and archive/common.rs:208-214.
- storage/scalar.rs:111 - `cast_slice::<T,u8>` of a possibly padded struct value exposes uninit padding bytes
  that nd_copy then moves with integer loads (also :125).
- storage/block.rs:193 - decoded length is only debug_asserted; in release a short zstd frame from a corrupt file
  leaves the tail of an uninit PoolBuf destination (storage/compact.rs:397) unwritten, then filters
  (codec/mod.rs:314-317) and copies read it.
- ops/where_op.rs:305 - condition bytes are read as `bool`; nothing found validating bool data decoded from an
  untrusted .jix file, so a byte value of 2 would be an invalid bool (outside this subsystem).

Non-test sizes: raw.rs 250, aligned_vec/mod.rs 453, buf_pool.rs 128, arrayvec.rs 614 (no tests), bitmap.rs 132,
hint.rs 23, cpu_cache.rs ~310 (tests at 156-171 and 328+), util/mod.rs 821. Hot spots above apply to all units.

### util-memory-alloc-pool (~830 lines)
- Files: jix/src/util/aligned_vec/raw.rs:1-250, jix/src/util/aligned_vec/mod.rs:1-453, jix/src/util/buf_pool.rs:1-128
- Consult: jix/src/codec/mod.rs (Encoder/Decoder/ReadContext), jix/src/storage/buf.rs, jix/src/array.rs:1280-1440,
  jix/src/storage/compact.rs:380-420, jix/src/dtype.rs:40-120 (Alignment), jix/src/util/cpu_cache.rs:233-326
- Focus: (1) every alloc/realloc/dealloc: size > 0, align a non-zero power of two, same Layout on alloc and dealloc
  on every path (grow from cap 0, shrink, clone, pool reuse)? (2) can align 0 reach RuntimeAlign/RawAlignedBytes?
  (3) shrink_to(0) / realloc failure. (4) does any consumer of `PoolBuf::as_*slice` or a pool-backed
  `StridedBuf::data()` treat the full capacity as the logical length? (5) is every PoolBuf / `set_len` byte
  written before it is read (short decode, filter tails, partial blocks)? (6) `get_pool` raw pointer across
  `align_other.insert`, reentrancy via PoolBuf Drop, `!Sync` really holding for ReadContext. (7) can the `size`
  passed to `get` wrap (32-bit, `product * itemsize`) while the strides describe the real shape?

### util-memory-arrayvec-bitmap-cache (~1100 lines)
